name: 夫が妻の姓を選ぶとき、それぞれの声

p_a471327a23.sentence: I was grateful that both sets of parents accepted my decision without taking it badly.
p_a471327a23.prev: They asked me again and again if I was really sure.
p_a471327a23.next: I still find it a little hard that I have less time to myself while living at my wife’s parents’ home.

p_db5f457aa1.sentence: Then I heard he would change his last name too, and I lost my composure.
p_db5f457aa1.prev: They’ll live near her parents’ home, much farther from us.
p_db5f457aa1.next: It felt like my son was moving away from me.

p_c9477d3e1a.sentence: I have to let go of my son, don’t I?
p_c9477d3e1a.prev: Someone told me that was old-fashioned, and I thought they were right.
p_c9477d3e1a.next: I still feel sad, but I want to accept his choice to take his wife’s last name.

p_ad9e388f65.sentence: That relative took his wife’s last name without talking it over with his parents first.
p_ad9e388f65.prev: If my son decided to do that, I wouldn’t oppose it, but I do think about a relative of mine.
p_ad9e388f65.next: I know his mother, my aunt, was so shocked that she became unwell.

p_bb5820f386.sentence: Even so, I don’t want to hold my son back because of my feelings as a parent.
p_bb5820f386.prev: I say the couple should decide for themselves, but that still bothers me.
p_bb5820f386.next: If he talked to me before choosing a last name, I could share how I feel.

p_785051cf57.sentence: When your last name changes after marriage, you think about both the name you’re used to hearing and your family ties, don’t you?
p_785051cf57.prev: What Each Person Says When a Husband Chooses His Wife’s Last Name
p_785051cf57.next: Whether a husband chooses his wife’s last name on the marriage form or becomes an adopted son-in-law, people have different feelings.

p_81fbbf59b8.sentence: My family is from a pretty rural area, but they don’t have old-fashioned views, and my parents accepted it without hesitation.
p_81fbbf59b8.prev: I had no problem at all with changing my last name.
p_81fbbf59b8.next: It was actually my wife’s parents who were more concerned.

p_71c2744709.sentence: But it was harder to adjust to the everyday ways of each family than to change my last name.
p_71c2744709.prev: I still find it a little hard that I have less time to myself while living at my wife’s parents’ home.
p_71c2744709.next: Once I could accept that it was natural for things to be different, I felt much better.

p_8243d757b0.sentence: I also want to keep some distance from his wife and put the couple’s happiness first.
p_8243d757b0.prev: I still feel sad, but I want to accept his choice to take his wife’s last name.
p_8243d757b0.next: Finally, we hear from someone in the parents’ generation who has a relative who chose his wife’s last name.

p_9ba97332d1.next: It was actually my wife’s parents who were more concerned.

p_35a522e9eb.prev: I think it’s fine for a man to choose his wife’s last name.
p_35a522e9eb.next: That relative took his wife’s last name without talking it over with his parents first.

p_f932b7703a.next: How should the things that matter to the person and their family be taken into account when making the decision?

p_d720d9c173.prev: That relative took his wife’s last name without talking it over with his parents first.
p_d720d9c173.next: Still, if my son’s future wife’s parents thought it was only natural, it would bother me.
